title: Operator Forensics and Non-Retention Exhibit (Draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This Exhibit defines obligations and procedures applicable to any Operator (vendor, subprocessor, or partner) that performs inference or otherwise processes Customer queries on behalf of Redwood Inference when those activities may produce or touch evidence relevant to security incidents, compliance audits, or legal process. The goal is to: (a) minimize retention of Customer-supplied inputs/outputs; (b) preserve high-fidelity forensic evidence when retention is necessary or requested; and (c) set predictable timelines and formats for evidence handback and validation.

Note: draft — this doc intentionally mixes legal clauses with technical implementation notes and TODOs for product/infra teams.

Key definitions (for Exhibit purposes):
- "Operator": party performing inference or operational support for inference on Redwood’s behalf (includes subprocessors).
- "Customer Material": any input, prompt, context, attachment, or generated output supplied by or derived from the Customer.
- "Forensic Evidence": logs, telemetry, KV cache snapshots, model-weight hashes, request/response payloads, system snapshots, chain-of-custody metadata, and any cryptographic proof necessary for verification.

Core commitments (Operator obligations):
1) Minimal retention principle:
- Operator will not persist Customer Material beyond the minimal technical lifetime required for immediate servicing (e.g., ephemeral KV cache for generation), unless a retention exception applies (see below).
- Default retention windows must be configurable per-customer; RL recommend default=24 hours for ephemeral caches and 7 days for short-term observability traces unless explicitly agreed.

2) Retention exceptions and approvals:
- Exceptions allowed only with prior written consent from Redwood’s Security team or pursuant to a lawful request (subpoena, court order).
- Every retention exception must be logged in an auditable register with: justification, scope (customer id, media type), retention window, approving party, and deletion verification method.

3) Forensic preservation on incident:
- If Redwood issues a preservation notice (Incident Preservation Notice) to the Operator, the Operator must: (a) immediately mark the relevant data as preserved; (b) create immutable copies of Forensic Evidence; (c) maintain chain-of-custody metadata (who/when/how the copy was created); (d) suspend any scheduled deletion of preserved items.
- Preservation notice timeframe: Operator must acknowledge within 2 business hours and confirm preservation actions within 24 hours.

4) Evidence handback and formats:
- Standard evidence delivery formats: compressed TAR/GZIP for files, newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) for logs, and cryptographic manifests (SHA-256) mapping file names to hashes.
- Time-to-delivery targets: initial evidence package within 72 hours of preserved-request; full forensic export (if requested) within 14 calendar days.
- Handback channels: secure transfer via SFTP with ephemeral keys, pre-shared encrypted object storage URLs, or Redwood’s approved E-Discovery connector.

5) Chain-of-custody and integrity:
- Operator must provide a manifest containing: file identifier, SHA-256 hash, creation timestamp (ISO8601), preservation trigger id, custodian identity (operator employee/service account), and a short audit trail (text).
- If HSM/KMS signing is available, packages should be signed with the Operator’s signing key and signature attached to the manifest.

6) Limited-use covenant:
- Forensic Evidence provided under preservation or handback will be used strictly for incident response, compliance validation, or legal obligations. Operator must not use this evidence for model re-training, product analytics, or any secondary purpose without explicit Redwood consent.

7) Subprocessor flow-down:
- Operator must flow these obligations to any subcontractor with the same or stricter controls and maintain a subprocessor register that Redwood can request.

8) Deletion verification:
- Upon expiry of a retention exception or at Redwood’s request after preservation is no longer required, Operator will perform deletion and provide deletion proof: secure delete command logs, overwritten file manifests, and updated manifests stamped with deletion timestamp and operator sign-off.

9) Failure modes and obligations:
- If Operator cannot meet a preservation or handback SLA, Operator must escalate to Redwood’s Security contact within 1 hour of breach, provide remediation plan, and accept credits or indemnities per primary agreement.

10) Audit and remote attestation:
- Redwood reserves the right to request evidence of controls via: (a) live remote attestation (minute-level judgment logs), (b) audit report snapshots (SOC2-like artifacts), or (c) onsite review under NDA.

Operational notes (implementation guidance, non-binding):
- Log sampling: for high-volume systems, preserve full traces for a 1:100 sampled set by default, unless Customer asks for full preservation. TODO: define sampling policy thresholds (tokens/sec, requests/min).
- Prefix/KV cache snapshots: store KV cache diffs with sequence IDs rather than full objects when possible to shrink packages. Include cache eviction metadata.
- Redaction guidance: where Customer requests, Operator should provide redacted copies plus an unredacted sealed copy accessible only via more rigorous legal process. Redaction must preserve structural metadata (message ids, timestamps) to maintain investigatory usefulness.

Unresolved items / actionables (notes to self):
- Decide default TTLs in infra config and expose per-customer override UI in Redwood Console. (Owner: Product; ETA: Q1 2026)
- Concur on 72h initial delivery window vs. 48h — security & legal to finalize.
- Template language for indemnity/credits to reference primary MSA clause X.Y. (Legal)
- Map to existing DPA retention and deletion obligations; ensure no conflict with Customer-specific DPA exceptions.

Sample clause for contract insertion (legal-friendly):
"Operator shall implement and maintain procedures and technical controls reasonably designed to ensure that Customer Material is not retained beyond the minimum necessary for processing, except where retention is explicitly authorized in writing by Redwood or as required by law. In the event Redwood issues a preservation notice, Operator shall immediately preserve and secure the relevant materials and deliver an initial evidence package in accordance with the timelines set forth in Exhibit [Forensics & Non-Retention]. Operator shall provide cryptographic manifests and chain-of-custody documentation for preserved materials and shall not use preserved materials for any purpose other than that authorized by Redwood or mandated by law."

Examples and scenarios (illustrative):
- Scenario A: security incident affecting 1 customer dataset — Operator preserves request logs and KV cache diffs for the customer, delivers ndjson logs + manifest within 48 hours.
- Scenario B: lawful process (subpoena) for narrow query — Operator marks the preserved set and coordinates handback via secure channel; scoped only to subpoena scope.

Appendix: Evidence package checklist (Operator to complete on delivery):
- [ ] Manifest (SHA-256 list)
- [ ] ndjson logs (compressed)
- [ ] KV cache snapshot or diffs (where applicable)
- [ ] System snapshot (service versions, kernel, docker/container id)
- [ ] Chain-of-custody note (text)
- [ ] Signed manifest (if HSM available)
- [ ] Decryption keys or key escrow metadata (if encrypted-at-rest for evidence)

Negotiation notes / fallback options:
- If Operator cannot produce SHA-256 manifest (legacy system), accept alternate hash (SHA-1) for initial delivery but require upgrade plan.
- If on-prem Operator cannot transfer large packages timely, accept staged delivery combined with remote access for triage.

Sign-off / signature block (placeholder):
- Redwood Inference (by: ______________________, name/title, date)
- Operator (by: ______________________, name/title, date)

End of draft.

---
Internal comments:
- This is intentionally prescriptive; legal can soften as needed. Keep the operational checklist — useful for SRE runbooks and third-party onboarding.
- Align with DPA exceptions and the "ephemeral kv" template in security playbooks.
